cases.source: Our teacher smiles and says see you tomorrow before closing the classroom door and carrying her books downstairs.
We should break the ice with a friendly introduction before discussing the serious problems in the schedule.
Maya asks me to spill the tea about the surprise party that everyone apparently organized without telling her.
I tell her the story is true, no cap, because I personally helped decorate the room before the guests arrived.
Nobody wants to throw shade at the organizer, although the unusual decorations provide plenty of opportunities for jokes.
Our British friend warns that we should not take the piss out of someone who seems genuinely upset.
The waiter spilled the tea across the tray, and the hot liquid soaked several paper napkins beside the cups.
The bottle has no cap on its neck, so the remaining water could easily spill inside the shopping bag.
A tall tree will throw shade across this terrace in summer, although there is almost no shade here today.
The atmosphere helps us break the ice with the new member of our group who moved here recently.
